keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for a rebel regime Cliopatria lacks (its Kamakura Shogunate row starts in 1188 and its Heian Japan row draws the whole realm to 1187). The land is the zone the heian-japan dossier gives the Genpei War's eastern front; the pages name Kamakura, Kai, Kōzuke and, on 9 November 1180, Suruga, never a boundary. The Kantō with Yamanashi is about 40,000 km2 by the gazetteer. No page gives an area.

ledger.note: 1180: the Minamoto rise in the east. The Genpei War runs from 20 June 1180 (infobox); Mochihito's call to arms went out in May and Yoritomo, beaten at Ishibashiyama in September (Yoritomo page), reached Kai and Kōzuke where 'the Takeda and other families helped repel the Taira'. No page dates the founding of a regime or lists its provinces.

ledger.note: 1180: Fujigawa, the first Minamoto victory. On 9 November 1180 the Minamoto clan with the Takeda of Kai beat the Taira at the Fuji River; Yoritomo was 'using Kamakura as his headquarters' and moved into Suruga. Mirrors the heian-japan east contest (1180).

region.text: the Kantō with Kai (Yamanashi): Yoritomo's base at Kamakura and the Takeda of Kai who joined him, as the heian-japan dossier draws the zone

ledger.note: 1185: the Genpei War ends. Infobox 'April 25, 1185', Minamoto victory, after Yashima and Dan-no-ura. The war was quiet for nearly two years from 1181 (Yoritomo page: a de facto truce 1181-1184 while he 'built an administration centered on his military headquarters in Kamakura').

region.text: the Kantō with Kai (Yamanashi): Yoritomo's base at Kamakura and the Takeda of Kai who joined him, as the heian-japan dossier draws the zone

ledger.note: 1185: Yoritomo's government becomes the Kamakura bakufu. In December 1185 Go-Shirakawa granted him the power 'to appoint stewards and constables in all provinces'; the Yoritomo page says he 'established the supremacy of the samurai and the first bakufu at Kamakura' in 1185, and the shogun title came in 1192.

notes: Written by jk-01-x on 2026-10-19 from three pages (Genpei War, Minamoto no Yoritomo, Battle of Fujigawa). Type rebel: the counterpart string 'Minamoto clan' in heian-japan (contest 1180-1185/4) is this slug. Thin on land: the pages name Kamakura (headquarters), Kai and Kōzuke (the Takeda and Nitta), and Suruga (Fujigawa, 9 November 1180); the Izu/Sagami/Musashi/Hitachi provinces are not on them, so the zone is the heian-japan dossier's Kantō + Yamanashi (confidence 2). Not drawn: Kiso Yoshinaka's separate rising in the north (Genpei page: 'had raised forces in the north'; Kyoto 1183, killed at Awazu 1184), the Taira's western court at Dazaifu and Yashima (heian-japan counterpart 'Taira clan (western court)', 1183-1185, two years: no dossier), the 1181-1183 lull. jk-01-a held the Kamakura bakufu to December 1185 (shugo and jitō); this dossier ends the same month. Disagreement: the Battle of Fujigawa page has Yoritomo at Kamakura already in August 1180, the Yoritomo page has him beaten at Ishibashiyama in September, in Awa, and raising a new army for about six months; the Yoritomo page also puts the first bakufu at Kamakura in 1185. Area comparison not applicable (no infobox area).
